To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) there is a significant performance gap between state-of-the-art algorithms and the performance needed for practical applications; (b) the performance gap is due to the fact that most algorithms are designed to work on controlled conditions, where the background is static and known, and the face is in a frontal pose; (c) the performance gap can be significantly closed by employing a novel set to video similarity measure, the matched background similarity, which can handle the challenges of real-world conditions

the best performing algorithms on the benchmark tests are based on the use of MBGS and that the current state of video face recognition performance is still far from the performance achieved on still images.
